title: All-stage finite-Tor pullback and the completed coefficient unit
statement:
Fix the purity coefficient datum [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,j}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^j$ for $j\geq1$. Work on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with the derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and finite-Tor constructible categories [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For a scheme $T$, the coefficient unit $\Lambda_T$ is $(A_{E,n})_T[0]$ at $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$, the completed sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}[0]$ at $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and its rationalized or common-stage image at $\Lambda=E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; the schemes themselves need not be separated over $k$. For every $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, derived pullback restricts to
$$
 Lf^*:D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)\longrightarrow D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda).
$$
At finite coefficients, if $K\in D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, then $Lf_n^*K$ is bounded constructible and has Tor amplitude in the same interval $[a,b]$. At integral coefficients, if $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ has every reduction $K_j=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,j}$ of Tor amplitude in one interval $[a,b]$ independent of $j$, then $Lf^*K$ is derived complete and bounded constructible, its canonical reduction is $(Lf^*K)_j\simeq Lf_j^*K_j$, and every reduction has Tor amplitude in that same interval. At the rational stage the restricted functor is integral pullback on representatives, and at the algebraically closed stage it is pullback on a common finite coefficient-field representative; at these two stages $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$.

There are canonical derived unit isomorphisms
$$
 u_{f,\Lambda}:Lf^*\Lambda_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_X.
$$
At finite level this is the exact inverse-image identification $f^{-1}(A_{E,n})_Y\simeq(A_{E,n})_X$. At integral level it is the map obtained by applying the specified derived inverse-limit construction of pullback to these compatible finite identifications:
$$
 Lf^*\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\simeq R\varprojlim_j\operatorname{Res}_j(A_{E,j})_X\simeq\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}.
$$
Here $\operatorname{Res}_j$ means restriction of coefficient scalars along $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,j}$, and the last isomorphism uses the finite reductions and derived completeness of the completed unit. At field stages $u_{f,\Lambda}$ is the rationalized or common-stage image of this integral unit isomorphism. These statements concern the actual completed coefficient sheaf, not the discrete constant integral sheaf, and include empty schemes.

proof.text: At every positive exponent n+1 apply sf_pullback_torAmplitude [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] to the given f, K and interval [a,b]. Its finite tensor-pullback presentation is identified with finiteDerivedPullback by openSquareDerivedPullbackModel [def-trf-finite-pullback-coordinate-comparison]. Bounded constructibility transports along this isomorphism by [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated]. Tor amplitude transports directly: a representative of the target, composed with the inverse isomorphism, is a representative of the source, so the same tensor-vanishing assertion applies. Unpack finiteTorConstructible and use the same interval to obtain the second finite-stage clause.

Derive invertibility of ell in residue fields from the purity base datum. Clause 1 of integralOperations_preserve_constructible [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] gives bounded constructibility of integral pullback and invertibility of integralPullbackFiniteComparison for every good representative. Choose a cochain representative by essential surjectivity of derived localization and resolve it by a flat-term K-flat complex [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Transport categorical termwise flatness to site flatness with siteSheafTensorRightIso [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits]. At level n compose the inverse-image reduction isomorphism as follows: asIso of integralPullbackFiniteComparison, localization of integralFinitePullbackModel [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], the exact-functor derived factorization, finite reduction on the K-flat representative [def-sf-finite-reduction-computation], and openSquareDerivedPullbackModel [def-trf-finite-pullback-coordinate-comparison]. This identifies the actual reduction of integral pullback with finiteDerivedPullback of the actual reduction of K. Constructibility of that input reduction comes from sfIntegralConstructible. Step 1 preserves its supplied Tor interval [a,b]; transport back along the composed isomorphism. Do this for all n with the same a,b. Retain the all-representatives IsIso assertion supplied by integralOperations_preserve_constructible. Finally unpack finiteTorConstructibleIntegral and reuse the same ordered interval to obtain its preservation.

Canonical finite reductions and constructible completeness for integral pullback on arbitrary schemes; the section-invariant unit presupposes the operations unit.
Generic canonical finite constant ring identification preserving constant sections, including the empty scheme.
Exactness of the same finite constant-coefficient module inverse image, used to compute its derived unit.
Regular completed module K-flatness and simultaneous quotient multiplication identifying the actual augmentations; equal-field specialization only.
Completeness of the actual rank-one regular completed module with its quotient projections on arbitrary schemes.
Specified functorial strict cone model for integral pullback, avoiding a noncanonical choice of a Roos-triangle map.
Natural tower-compatible scalar comparisons already specified by the common-stage pullback definition.
Membership of the completed unit and of its rationalized and common-stage images in the constructible categories, so that the unit pullbacks are defined there; no purity-conventions node states it.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q55-d65b16909 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: First split of the Q115 node; the statement is byte-identical, and stmt_deps only gain the rational and common-stage definitions that the statement uses. There are no new nodes. I read all six steps against the full statements of the cited nodes, the blueprint def-pur-section-invariant (main-20261015) and Bhatt-Scholze 6.5.9(4)(5). Step 1: lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude has exactly the hypotheses here (separated finite-type map, finite-type schemes, which need not be separated over k). Step 2: preserve-constructible (1) needs only that ell is invertible; it gives (Lf^*K)_j = f^{-1}K_j = Lf_j^*K_j, and the interval [a,b] is uniform in j. Step 3: the constant ring map plus exactness give the finite units; they commute with the transitions because maps out of a sheafified constant sheaf are determined on constant sections. Step 4: with the strict unit at L=E and free-cell completeness, the augmentation is an isomorphism, and any lift of the projections is unique since Ext^{-1}=0. Step 5: the explicit cone of 1-s is mapped isomorphically by the tower isomorphism. Step 6: rational and Qbar images under the operations definition. Fault (C1/C4), repaired: membership of the completed unit O^_W[0] in D^b_c(W,O_E), and of E_W and (Qbar)_W in their categories, was asserted without a citation; it is needed for integral Lf^* to be defined on the unit. Fix: cite lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible (1)(2) in step 4 and (3) in step 6, add it to proof_deps and to tool_uses, and touch nothing else. Edge cases checked: f=id, empty schemes, K=0, n=1, a non-separated X. lem-pur-completed-unit-pullback-tower is correctly not cited because it assumes separated schemes. Batch-5 flag: lem-pod-completed-integral-scalar-regular is a general fact (multiplication by varpi^m is injective on sections of the completed sheaf). It is not part of the trace formula or of Poincare duality, and it was already in the closure of the item's stmt_deps, so I accept it. No SGA is cited and there is no cycle.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
